title: Happy the Birth Where Grace Presides
description: Happy the Birth Where Grace Presides in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 60, “The power of grace”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hap-py the birth where grace pre-sides To form the fu-ture life! In wis-dom's paths the soul she guides, Re-mote from noise and strife.

lines: Happy the birth where grace presides
To form the future life!
In wisdom's paths the soul she guides,
Remote from noise and strife.
Since I have known the Savior's name
And what for me he bore;
No more I toil for empty fame,
I thirst for gold no more.
Placed by his hand in this retreat,
I make his love my theme;
And see that all the world calls great,
Is but a waking dream.
Since be has ranked my worthless name
Amongst his favored few;
Let the mad world who scoff at them
Revile and hate me too.
O thou whose voice the dead can raise,
And soften hearts of stone,
And teach the dumb to sing thy praise,
This work is all thine own!
Thy wond'ring saints rejoice to see
A wretch, like me, restored
And point, and say, "How changed is he,
Who once defied the Lord!"
Grace bid me live, and taught my tongue
To aim at notes divine;
And grace accepts my feeble song,
The glory, Lord, be thine!

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
